finding.claim: Form-urlencoded request bodies are not parsed (no ARGS_POST, no REQUEST_BODY) when Content-Type carries a parameter such as `; charset=UTF-8`, so body rules on ARGS and REQUEST_BODY never see the payload under default configuration. The backend framework will still parse the same body as a form.
finding.source: Remote HTTP client. Precondition: default WAF config (RequestBodyAccess on, no ctl:requestBodyProcessor, ForceRequestBodyVariable false) and a Content-Type header value of `application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=UTF-8` (or any other parameter suffix).
finding.sink: Body processing is skipped, so the body-phase rules evaluate with empty ARGS_POST and REQUEST_BODY. The protected application still parses the form, so injected payloads (SQLi, XSS, command injection in form fields) reach it uninspected.

trace.note: AddRequestHeader switches on the lowercased header name `content-type`.
val = strings.ToLower(value). The full header value is kept, including parameters.
Exact equality `val == "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"`. With `; charset=...` this is false, so reqbodyProcessor is not set to URLENCODED.
The multipart branch uses HasPrefix, so multipart/form-data with parameters is handled. The urlencoded branch is inconsistent with it.
ProcessRequestBody reads rbp from reqbodyProcessor, which is empty.
The default-processor fallback runs only when ForceRequestBodyVariable is true. It defaults to false, reset per transaction at internal/corazawaf/waf.go:210.
rbp == "" leads to Rules.Eval(PhaseRequestBody) with no body processor run. ARGS_POST and REQUEST_BODY stay empty.
The URL-encoded processor that would populate ARGS_POST and REQUEST_BODY is never invoked for this request.

finding.guards_checked: (1) Content-Type parameters are stripped elsewhere: transaction.go:499 and :427 use strings.Cut, and the request-body write path at :512 uses the same Cut, so the inconsistency is local to line 386. (2) Other paths that set URLENCODED: only ctl:requestBodyProcessor (internal/actions/ctl.go, config-driven, not attacker-controlled) and transaction.go:1113 under ForceRequestBodyVariable. Neither applies to a default deployment. (3) Tests: transaction_test.go:250, :1836 and body_test.go:24,45 use only the exact media type, so the parameterised form is untested. seclang/rules_test.go:792 shows the project expects `; charset=` to be normal. (4) Body-limit logic (transaction.go:906-1053) is consistent and not implicated.
